lines:
Three fixes implemented and verified.

1. provider_tools/openai.rs - a renderer guard: an exchange whose assistant content has neither text nor a tool call contributes no assistant message, so a reasoning-only turn already committed in a stored transcript replays instead of making every later request invalid. This is what unblocks chat.0e61d222be0b04c2ee63ff7c1c0edd14d085e98f.
2. model_tool_loop/empty_turn.rs - recover() commits a turn only when it carries assistant text or a tool call (is_resendable); reasoning alone is never committed.
3. model_tool_loop.rs - ProviderRecoveryBudget now tracks the consecutive identical failure and its count (progressed() clears the streak on any accepted turn). Five in a row, with no successful turn in between, ends the pass and reports why: "The provider refused this exact request N times in a row, so no turn reached the model." Below the threshold nothing changes: every failure is still reported and the model still decides.

VERIFICATION (all run with a writable TMP/TEMP)
- cargo check --tests: clean, no new warnings.
- capability-host lib: 188 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, including the new provider_tools::reasoning_passback_tests::a_reasoning_only_turn_contributes_no_assistant_message.
- capability-host integration: provider_tools_openai 3/3, provider_protocols 2/2, provider_images 4/4, milestone and host suites green.
- desktop model_tool_loop: 14/14, including the new an_identically_repeating_provider_failure_ends_the_pass_instead_of_spinning and the adapted a_short_run_of_unchanged_failures_is_reported_and_the_model_still_answers.
- desktop compaction_integration: 31/31 (the #191 prefix-cache work is unaffected).
- desktop pipeline: 88/89; the single failure (standard_agent_workflow_runs_plan_agent_output_wait_end_to_end) passes once USERPROFILE is set, so it is the shell's missing home directory, not this change.
- desktop an_accepted_turn_with_no_answer_is_reported_and_the_run_continues: passes.

AUDIT CAVEATS / NOT DONE
- The failure-policy design spec aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy still states "no limit ends a run; every condition is reported". Fix 3 is a deliberate, user-requested exception and the spec was not amended in this change, so model and code disagree until it is. docs/context-compaction.md has the same sentence.
- The provider's own 400 diagnostic body is still not captured; the run records "provider returned HTTP status 400" and the new failure text. Surfacing the provider message would make the next diagnosis faster.
- Not investigated further: whether DeepSeek's 64K ceiling can be raised by sending an explicit max_tokens; the recorded parameters carried none, so the ceiling was the provider's default.

Follow-up to #191 from the second benchmark run (chat.0e61d222be0b04c2ee63ff7c1c0edd14d085e98f, 4,529 events, stopped by the user).

WHAT HAPPENED
- Turn 1 hit the provider's response ceiling: 65,536 output tokens, all of it reasoning, no assistant text and no tool call.
- The #191 empty-turn fix committed that turn as an exchange. The OpenAI-compatible renderer wrote {"role":"assistant","content":null} with no tool_calls, and the provider answered HTTP 400 to every later request.
- The provider-error recovery then re-dispatched the identical request 335 times in ~3 minutes (span.model turn.2 .. turn.335, ~0.6 s apart, no usage recorded), piling the recovery notice up to ~200 copies before bound_model_notice truncated it. The user stopped the run. Nothing would have stopped it by itself: no report budget may end a node, by design.

WHY THERE WAS A "LIMIT"
- There is no Aworkit output cap on an Agent node. The recorded wire parameters were {"reasoningEffort":"high"}; max_tokens is only written when maxOutputTokens resolves (provider_tools/openai.rs apply). The model's declared maxOutputTokens (393,216) feeds the compaction budget, not the agent turn. 65,536 is the provider's own response ceiling for that model.
- The count that made no sense was our own: MAXIMUM_ERROR_RECOVERIES (32) changed only the notice wording and never stopped anything, so an identically failing dispatch could repeat for ever.

FIXES
1. provider_tools/openai.rs: an exchange with neither text nor a tool call contributes no assistant message, so a reasoning-only turn already stored in a transcript replays instead of poisoning every later request (this also unblocks the chat that is stuck).
2. model_tool_loop/empty_turn.rs: recover() commits a turn only when it carries assistant text or a tool call; reasoning alone is never committed.
3. model_tool_loop.rs: ProviderRecoveryBudget tracks consecutive identical failures. Five in a row with no successful turn in between ends the pass with a reported reason ("The provider refused this exact request N times in a row, so no turn reached the model"); any successful turn clears the streak. This is the "detect that the same call keeps failing" behaviour the user asked for.

POLICY NOTE / OPEN ITEM
- Fix 3 deliberately adds a fourth stopping condition, which contradicts the normative design spec aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy ("no limit ends a run; every condition is reported"). It is justified as a fact about the dispatch rather than a budget on the work (no request reaches the model, so no Agent decision is pending), but the design spec and docs/context-compaction.md still state the old rule and should be amended to record this exception.

data.title: Stop the identical-provider-failure retry loop, and never commit a reasoning-only assistant turn
